doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Her father's support and her Grammy nomination
summary: Her father backed her lyric writing; she wishes her parents had seen her Grammy nomination.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Nice. To wrap up, I’m wondering if your parents lived long enough to see your path come to fruition?

My dad came to some gigs at which I was doing all my own songs. And he got a huge kick out of it because people would come up to him and say, “Oh Leonard, the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree.” He was a huge supporter of my lyric writing ambitions and in fact when he was in the hospital in Encino Tarzana Hospital and very sick, I remember him saying, “Did you send Cleo Laine your Ellington re-dos? Because she’s doing an Ellington album with Mercer Ellington. Did you send them to her?” And I was able to go, “Yes. She got back to me, she’s recording a couple of them.” He cared a lot about my writing and we went to ASCAP meetings together. He was very proud of me. But when I got my first Grammy nomination I cried a bit because I wished they could have seen that. It would have been exciting even though my dad had something of a jaundiced view of awards and ceremonies. But he would have been so proud.
